questions.question: Who is subject to the dietary supplement CGMP requirements of 21 CFR Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Manufacture, package, label, or hold a dietary supplement; includes those who hold for distribution; excludes certain retailers/holders as specified.

questions.question: Where are the definitions that apply to 21 CFR Part 111 located, and does Part 111 incorporate definitions from elsewhere?
questions.key_answer_elements: Definitions section for Part 111; also incorporates FD&C Act and Part 1 definitions by reference.

questions.question: What personnel qualification requirements apply under the Part 111 personnel subpart?
questions.key_answer_elements: Qualified persons, education/training/experience, supervisor requirements.

questions.question: What hygienic practices must employees follow under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Handwashing, outer garments, jewelry, eating/drinking restrictions, disease control.

questions.question: What records must be made and kept under the Part 111 personnel subpart, and where are the general recordkeeping requirements for those records found?
questions.key_answer_elements: Subpart B records requirement plus Subpart P general records/retention rules.

questions.question: What sanitation requirements apply to the physical plant and grounds under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Litter/waste, pest control, cleaning, sanitizing agents, toilet facilities, plumbing.

questions.question: What are the water supply requirements for a dietary supplement facility?
questions.key_answer_elements: Water that contacts components/product or contact surfaces must be safe and sanitary quality.

questions.question: What design and construction requirements apply to the physical plant under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Suitable size/construction/design, separation of operations, lighting, ventilation, floors/walls/ceilings.

questions.question: What requirements apply to automated, mechanical, or electronic equipment used in dietary supplement manufacturing?
questions.key_answer_elements: Design/installation for intended use, calibration, backup, controls to prevent unauthorized changes.

questions.question: What is the requirement to establish a production and process control system under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Establish and follow written procedures covering all stages of manufacturing, packaging, labeling, holding.

questions.question: What specifications must a dietary supplement manufacturer establish?
questions.key_answer_elements: Component, in-process, packaging/label, finished batch, and product-received specifications.

questions.question: A finished batch fails an identity specification. What does Part 111 require the firm to do, and who makes the disposition decision?
questions.key_answer_elements: Determine whether specs are met, quality control personnel material review and disposition, treatment of deviations, reprocessing limits.

questions.question: What representative samples must be collected under Part 111, and what reserve sample requirements apply?
questions.key_answer_elements: Representative samples of components, packaging, labels, in-process, finished batch; reserve sample size, storage conditions, retention period.

questions.question: What must quality control personnel do under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Review and approve/reject, review records, perform material review and disposition, approve deviations and reprocessing.

questions.question: Under Part 111, what is the difference between the responsibilities of quality control personnel and those of production personnel?
questions.key_answer_elements: QC independence, approval authority, separation of duties, no self-approval of own work.

questions.question: What requirements apply to components, packaging, and labels before use in dietary supplement manufacturing?
questions.key_answer_elements: Identity verification of each component, supplier COA reliance conditions, quarantine, rejection of unsuitable materials.

questions.question: A firm wants to rely on a supplier certificate of analysis instead of testing a component for identity. Is that allowed?
questions.key_answer_elements: Identity test of a dietary ingredient by the manufacturer is required; COA reliance permitted for other component specs only after qualifying the supplier and periodic reconfirmation.

questions.question: What must the master manufacturing record include under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Name/strength/concentration, batch size, complete list of components, accurate statement of weight/measure, identity statement, procedures, specifications at each point, in-process controls, packaging/labeling.

questions.question: When is a master manufacturing record required, and how does it relate to the batch production record?
questions.key_answer_elements: MMR required for each unique formulation and batch size; BPR must accurately follow the MMR.

questions.question: What must the batch production record contain under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Batch/lot identification, identity/weight/measure of each component, dates and times, equipment used, initials of persons performing and verifying, results of tests, documentation of deviations.

questions.question: What must laboratory control processes include under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Sample use, criteria for selecting test methods, sampling plans, criteria for accepting/rejecting test results.

questions.question: What requirements apply to laboratory methods for testing and examination under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Methods must be appropriate and scientifically valid; verification of suitability for the matrix.

questions.question: What manufacturing operations requirements apply under Part 111 to prevent contamination?
questions.key_answer_elements: Sanitation, protection against contamination, control of physical/chemical/microbial hazards during manufacturing.

questions.question: What packaging and labeling operations requirements apply under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Package/label suitability, label examination, filling/assembling/packaging controls, gang printing controls, label reconciliation.

questions.question: What holding and distributing requirements apply under Part 111?
questions.key_answer_elements: Holding under appropriate conditions, holding of reserve samples, distribution under conditions protecting against deterioration.

questions.question: A distributor returns a dietary supplement. What does Part 111 require the manufacturer to do with it?
questions.key_answer_elements: Identify and quarantine, QC review, destruction or reprocessing conditions, salvage limits, investigation of other batches.

questions.question: What must a firm do when it receives a product complaint about a dietary supplement?
questions.key_answer_elements: QC personnel review, determine whether complaint involves a possible CGMP failure, investigate, record required information.

questions.question: How long must Part 111 records be retained and how must they be made available?
questions.key_answer_elements: Retention period tied to date of manufacture/expiration; available for FDA inspection and copying; original or true copy.

questions.question: Who is subject to 21 CFR Part 117 and what are the principal exemptions?
questions.key_answer_elements: Exemptions for certain facilities/activities, juice and seafood HACCP, low-risk on-farm activities, qualified facilities.

questions.question: What is a 'qualified facility' under Part 117 and what modified requirements apply to one?
questions.key_answer_elements: Definition tied to average annual sales thresholds, modified requirements in lieu of a full food safety plan.

questions.question: What CGMP requirements apply to personnel under Part 117 Subpart B?
questions.key_answer_elements: Disease control, cleanliness, hand washing, jewelry, glove use, hair restraints.

questions.question: What sanitation requirements apply to plant and grounds under Part 117 Subpart B?
questions.key_answer_elements: Grounds maintenance, plant construction and design, sanitary operations, cleaning and sanitizing, pest control.

questions.question: What requirements apply to equipment and utensils under Part 117 Subpart B?
questions.key_answer_elements: Design, materials, workmanship, seams, temperature-measuring devices, compressed air and gases.

questions.question: What are the Part 117 CGMP requirements for warehousing and distribution?
questions.key_answer_elements: Storage and transport under conditions protecting against contamination and deterioration.

questions.question: What must a food safety plan contain under Part 117?
questions.key_answer_elements: Hazard analysis, preventive controls, supply-chain program, recall plan, monitoring, corrective action, verification procedures.

questions.question: What does the hazard analysis requirement of Part 117 require a facility to evaluate?
questions.key_answer_elements: Identification of known or reasonably foreseeable biological, chemical, and physical hazards; hazard evaluation for severity and probability.

questions.question: What is the difference between a process preventive control, a sanitation preventive control, and an allergen preventive control under Part 117?
questions.key_answer_elements: Categories of preventive controls, written procedures, parameters and values, application to identified hazards.

questions.question: What are the monitoring requirements for preventive controls under Part 117?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written procedures, monitoring as appropriate to the control, documentation in records.

questions.question: A metal detector fails mid-shift at a food facility. What does Part 117 require regarding corrective actions and corrections?
questions.key_answer_elements: Corrective action procedures, identify and correct, evaluate affected food, prevent recurrence, distinguish corrections from corrective actions, records.

questions.question: What verification activities does Part 117 require?
questions.key_answer_elements: Validation, verification of monitoring and corrective actions, calibration, product testing, environmental monitoring, reanalysis, records review.

questions.question: When must a facility reanalyze its food safety plan under Part 117?
questions.key_answer_elements: At least every three years, and when a significant change, new hazard, unanticipated food safety problem, or ineffective control is found.

questions.question: What are the recall plan requirements under Part 117?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written recall plan for foods with a hazard requiring a preventive control, notification, effectiveness checks, disposition.

questions.question: Who is a preventive controls qualified individual and what must that person do?
questions.key_answer_elements: PCQI definition, required training or job experience, preparation of the food safety plan, validation, records review.

questions.question: What modified requirements apply to a qualified facility under Part 117 Subpart D?
questions.key_answer_elements: Attestation submissions to FDA, either hazard-control attestation or compliance-with-state-law attestation, records.

questions.question: What requirements apply to the storage of unexposed packaged food that requires time/temperature control under Part 117 Subpart D?
questions.key_answer_elements: Temperature controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, records for refrigerated packaged food.

questions.question: How may FDA withdraw a qualified facility exemption under Part 117?
questions.key_answer_elements: Circumstances, order to withdraw, compliance and appeal procedures, reinstatement.

questions.question: What are the general recordkeeping requirements under Part 117, including retention period?
questions.key_answer_elements: Required record elements, signature/date, retention of at least two years, offsite storage rules, availability to FDA.

questions.question: What must a supply-chain program include under Part 117 Subpart G?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written program, use of approved suppliers, supplier verification activities, determining appropriate verification, records.

questions.question: A receiving facility identifies a hazard in a raw material controlled by its supplier. What supplier verification activities does Part 117 allow, and how is the appropriate one selected?
questions.key_answer_elements: Onsite audit, sampling and testing, review of supplier food safety records; selection based on hazard severity and supplier performance; annual onsite audit for SAHCODHA hazards.

questions.question: How does the Part 117 supply-chain program differ from the FSVP requirements for importers?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR 117 Subpart G; 21 CFR 1 Subpart L
questions.key_answer_elements: Domestic receiving facility vs importer obligations, overlap and non-duplication provisions.

questions.question: What are the principal display panel requirements for a food label?
questions.key_answer_elements: PDP definition and area, information panel placement, type size, prominence.

questions.question: How must the statement of identity appear on a food label?
questions.key_answer_elements: Bold type on the PDP, common or usual name, form of the food, size relative to the most prominent printed matter.

questions.question: How must ingredients be declared on a food label?
questions.key_answer_elements: Descending order of predominance by weight, common or usual names, sub-ingredient declarations, color and spice declarations.

questions.question: What must the name and place of business declaration include?
questions.key_answer_elements: Firm name, street address (with conditions for omission), city, state, ZIP; qualifying phrase when not the manufacturer.

questions.question: How must net quantity of contents be declared?
questions.key_answer_elements: Location in lower 30 percent of PDP, type size by PDP area, dual declaration metric and US customary.

questions.question: What are the requirements for declaring serving size on the Nutrition Facts label?
questions.key_answer_elements: RACC basis, household measure plus metric, dual-column requirements, single-serving container rules.

questions.question: Which nutrients are mandatory in the Nutrition Facts panel and what are the rounding rules?
questions.key_answer_elements: Mandatory nutrient list, added sugars, vitamin D and potassium, increment and rounding rules per nutrient.

questions.question: A product is packaged in a container that holds between 200 and 300 percent of the RACC. How must the Nutrition Facts be presented?
questions.key_answer_elements: Dual-column labeling per serving and per container requirements and exemptions.

questions.question: What are the small-package labeling exemptions and alternatives in Part 101?
questions.key_answer_elements: Exemptions by package size and firm size, tabular and linear display formats, low-volume exemption notice.

questions.question: How must major food allergens be declared on a food label?
questions.key_answer_elements: Contains statement or parenthetical in ingredient list, the nine major allergens including sesame.

questions.question: What conditions apply to nutrient content claims such as 'low sodium' or 'good source'?
questions.key_answer_elements: General principles, defined criteria per claim, disclosure statements, referenced food requirements.

questions.question: What is the difference between a health claim, a qualified health claim, and a structure/function claim?
questions.key_answer_elements: Authorized health claim standard, significant scientific agreement, qualified claim disclaimers, structure/function notification and disclaimer.

questions.question: What are the specific requirements for the labeling of dietary supplements, including the Supplement Facts panel?
questions.key_answer_elements: Supplement Facts format, dietary ingredient listing, proprietary blends, part of plant, serving size.

questions.question: What must a structure/function claim on a dietary supplement include, and what must be submitted to FDA?
questions.key_answer_elements: Required disclaimer text, notification to FDA within 30 days of first marketing, substantiation.

questions.question: When must a food bear a common or usual name established by regulation, and where are those names codified?
questions.key_answer_elements: Common or usual name principles, relationship between Part 101 and Part 102.

questions.question: What are the requirements for nutrition labeling of restaurant and vending machine foods?
questions.key_answer_elements: Covered establishments, standard menu items, calorie declaration, additional written nutrition information.

questions.question: What is the scope of 21 CFR Part 211 and how does it relate to Part 210?
questions.key_answer_elements: Minimum CGMP for finished pharmaceuticals, applicability, relationship to other regulations and to Part 210 definitions.

questions.question: What are the responsibilities of the quality control unit?
questions.key_answer_elements: Authority to approve/reject components, drug products, procedures and specifications; written procedures; adequate laboratory facilities.

questions.question: What are the personnel qualification and training requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Education/training/experience, CGMP training on a continuing basis, adequate number of qualified personnel, supervisor qualifications.

questions.question: What are the consultant requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Sufficient education, training, experience; records of name, address, qualifications, and service provided.

questions.question: What building and facility requirements apply to aseptic processing areas?
questions.key_answer_elements: Separate or defined areas, floors/walls/ceilings smooth and cleanable, HEPA-filtered air under positive pressure, environmental monitoring, air pressure differential systems.

questions.question: What are the ventilation, air filtration, and air heating/cooling requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Adequate ventilation, control of air pressure, microorganisms, dust, humidity and temperature, filtration for penicillin and other sensitive areas.

questions.question: What are the equipment cleaning and maintenance requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Cleaning and maintenance at appropriate intervals, written procedures, cleaning records, assignment of responsibility.

questions.question: What requirements apply to automatic, mechanical, and electronic equipment used in drug manufacturing?
questions.key_answer_elements: Calibration and checks, written program, input/output verification, control over changes, backup of records.

questions.question: What testing and approval requirements apply to incoming components under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Representative sampling, identity test on each lot, supplier COA reliance conditions, retest intervals, rejection criteria.

questions.question: What are the requirements for use of approved components and for rejected components?
questions.key_answer_elements: FIFO/stock rotation, retesting of components, control of rejected materials.

questions.question: What written procedures are required for production and process control?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written procedures for production and process control designed to assure identity, strength, quality, and purity; deviations recorded and justified.

questions.question: What charge-in of components controls does Part 211 require?
questions.key_answer_elements: Weighing and measuring, verification by a second person, identification of containers, accuracy of component addition.

questions.question: What are the yield calculation and reconciliation requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Actual yields and percentages of theoretical yield at appropriate phases, performed and verified by second person.

questions.question: What are the in-process sampling and testing requirements?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written procedures, control procedures to monitor output and validate performance, in-process specifications, rejected in-process material handling.

questions.question: What requirements apply to time limitations on production and to the control of microbiological contamination?
questions.key_answer_elements: Established time limits for each phase, written procedures to prevent objectionable microorganisms, validation of sterilization processes.

questions.question: What are the requirements for labeling issuance and control?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written procedures for receipt, identification, storage, handling, sampling, examination; issuance and reconciliation of labels; gang printing restrictions.

questions.question: What are the drug product inspection and expiration dating requirements?
questions.key_answer_elements: Packaged and labeled product examination, expiration date determined by stability testing, appearance on labeling.

questions.question: What holding and distribution requirements apply under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Quarantine before release, storage conditions, written distribution procedures, oldest stock distributed first, recall facilitation.

questions.question: What are the general laboratory control requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Scientifically sound specifications and test procedures, approval by the quality control unit, calibration of instruments.

questions.question: What testing and release requirements apply before distribution of a drug product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Testing for identity and strength of each active ingredient, sampling plans, statistical criteria, validated analytical methods.

questions.question: What is required by the stability testing regulation?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written stability program, sample size and test intervals, storage conditions, reliable and specific test methods, testing of the drug in the same container-closure.

questions.question: What are the reserve sample requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Reserve samples of active ingredients and drug product, quantity twice that needed for all required tests, retention periods, visual examination.

questions.question: An HPLC assay result is out of specification. What does Part 211 require, and what does the Barr decision framework add?
questions.key_answer_elements: Thorough failure investigation, extension to other batches, written conclusion and follow-up; Phase I laboratory investigation and Phase II full-scale investigation; no invalidation without assignable cause.

questions.question: What are the general requirements for records and reports under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Retention of at least one year past expiration date, availability for inspection, annual product review requirement, record system.

questions.question: What is the difference between the master production record and the batch production record?
questions.key_answer_elements: Master record content and independent verification; batch record as reproduction of the master with actual execution documentation.

questions.question: What must the production record review include, and who must perform it?
questions.key_answer_elements: Review and approval by the quality control unit before release, investigation of any unexplained discrepancy or batch failure.

questions.question: What are the complaint file requirements under Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written procedures, review by the quality control unit, determination of whether a report under Part 310 or 314 is required, record contents and retention.

questions.question: What are the requirements for returned and salvaged drug products?
questions.key_answer_elements: Identification and holding, destruction unless testing supports suitability, salvage limited to specified conditions with records.

questions.question: What is the scope of 21 CFR Part 820 and which manufacturers are subject to it?
questions.iso_clause_title: Scope; Quality management system — General requirements
questions.key_answer_elements: Design, manufacture, packaging, labeling, storage, installation, servicing of finished devices for human use; QMS appropriate to the specific device.

questions.question: Are manufacturers of components and parts of finished devices subject to 21 CFR Part 820?
questions.key_answer_elements: Component and part manufacturers are outside the scope; FDA encourages voluntary application.

questions.question: Are manufacturers of blood and blood components subject to 21 CFR Part 820?
questions.key_answer_elements: Blood and blood components are excluded from Part 820; those manufacturers are subject to Part 606.

questions.question: Are human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products regulated as devices subject to Part 820, and what else applies to them?
questions.key_answer_elements: HCT/Ps regulated as devices are in scope of Part 820 and are also subject to Part 1271; the specifically applicable regulation supersedes the more general one.

questions.question: If a requirement of ISO 13485 conflicts with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act or another FDA regulation, which one governs?
questions.key_answer_elements: Conflicts provision: the FD&C Act and the applicable FDA regulations govern over the incorporated standard.

questions.question: What does Part 820 provide with respect to foreign manufacturers that refuse to permit an FDA inspection?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR 820.1(c); section 801(a) of the FD&C Act
questions.key_answer_elements: Refusal to permit inspection is grounds for refusal of admission of the device into the United States.

questions.question: How may a manufacturer obtain an exemption or variance from a requirement of Part 820?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR 820.1(d); section 520(f) of the FD&C Act; 21 CFR 10.30
questions.key_answer_elements: Exemption or variance under section 520(f)(2); requested by citizen petition under 10.30.

questions.question: Which definitions apply to 21 CFR Part 820, and what takes precedence when terms conflict?
questions.key_answer_elements: ISO 13485 definitions apply except as superseded by 820.3; ISO 9000:2015 Clause 3 separately incorporated; FD&C Act section 201 definitions supersede correlating standard terms.

questions.question: What meaning does Part 820 give to the term 'safety and performance' as it is used in the incorporated standard?
questions.key_answer_elements: 'Safety and performance' carries the meaning of 'safety and effectiveness' as used in the FD&C Act and FDA regulations.

questions.question: Which standards and editions does 21 CFR Part 820 incorporate by reference, and for which sections is each approved?
questions.iso_clause_title: Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes; Terms and definitions
questions.key_answer_elements: ISO 13485:2016(E), third edition, March 1, 2016 — IBR approved for 820.1, 820.3, 820.10, 820.35 and 820.45; ISO 9000:2015(E) Clause 3 — IBR approved for 820.3.

questions.question: If ISO publishes a new edition of ISO 13485, does that new edition automatically become the standard required by Part 820?
questions.iso_clause_title: Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes
questions.key_answer_elements: No. Incorporation by reference fixes the 2016 third edition until FDA amends the regulation; a later edition does not apply automatically.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR 820.10 require of a manufacturer subject to Part 820?
questions.iso_clause_title: Quality management system; Management responsibility; Resource management; Product realization; Measurement, analysis and improvement
questions.key_answer_elements: Document a QMS that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485 and the other applicable requirements of Part 820.

questions.question: Which section of Part 820 links the identification requirements of the incorporated standard to unique device identification, and which part sets those UDI requirements?
questions.key_answer_elements: A documented system to assign unique device identification must be maintained in accordance with Part 830.

questions.question: Which section of Part 820 links traceability to the device tracking requirements of Title 21, and which part applies?
questions.key_answer_elements: Documented traceability procedures required in accordance with the device tracking requirements of Part 821.

questions.question: Under Part 820, where must complaints meeting the medical device reporting criteria be reported, and which section establishes that link?
questions.key_answer_elements: Complaints meeting the reporting criteria of Part 803 must be reported to FDA.

questions.question: How must advisory notices be handled under Part 820, and which section establishes that requirement?
questions.iso_clause_title: Communication; Reporting to regulatory authorities; Actions in response to nonconforming product detected after delivery
questions.key_answer_elements: Advisory notices must be handled in accordance with the corrections and removals requirements of Part 806.

questions.question: Which devices must apply the design and development requirements of the incorporated standard, and which section of Part 820 states that?
questions.key_answer_elements: Mandatory for Class II and Class III devices and for the Class I devices listed in 820.10(c).

questions.question: How does Part 820 extend the standard's traceability requirements for implantable devices beyond the standard's own scope?
questions.iso_clause_title: Traceability — Particular requirements for implantable medical devices
questions.key_answer_elements: FDA extends the implantable-device traceability clause to devices that support or sustain life and whose failure can be reasonably expected to result in a significant injury.

questions.question: What is the consequence under Part 820 of failing to comply with the quality management system requirements?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR 820.10(e); section 501(h) of the FD&C Act
questions.key_answer_elements: The device is adulterated and the manufacturer is subject to enforcement action.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR 820.35 add to the record control requirements of the incorporated standard?
questions.key_answer_elements: FDA supplement specifying additional required record content beyond the standard's record control clause.

questions.question: What must be recorded for complaints involving the possible failure of a device, labeling, or packaging to meet specifications?
questions.key_answer_elements: Records of review, evaluation and investigation, including the justification when no investigation is made.

questions.question: What minimum data elements must a servicing record contain under Part 820?
questions.key_answer_elements: Six specified elements including device name, unique device identifier or other identification, date of service, individual servicing the device, service performed, and test and inspection data.

questions.question: What does Part 820 require with respect to recording the unique device identifier, and which record control section states it?
questions.iso_clause_title: Control of production and service provision; Identification; Traceability
questions.key_answer_elements: The UDI must be recorded for each medical device or batch of medical devices.

questions.question: How may a manufacturer indicate to FDA that a record it holds is confidential?
questions.key_answer_elements: Records deemed confidential may be marked to aid FDA in determining whether the information may be disclosed.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR 820.45 require that the incorporated standard does not?
questions.iso_clause_title: Control of production and service provision
questions.key_answer_elements: Documented procedures for activities ensuring the integrity of device labeling and packaging, supplementing the standard's production control clause.

questions.question: What examination of labeling and packaging is required before release or storage under Part 820?
questions.iso_clause_title: Control of production and service provision
questions.key_answer_elements: Labeling and packaging must be examined for accuracy prior to release or storage.

questions.question: What must be documented when labeling is released for use?
questions.key_answer_elements: Release of labeling for use must be documented.

questions.question: What controls does Part 820 require over labeling and packaging operations to prevent mixups, and what must be documented?
questions.iso_clause_title: Medical device file; Control of records
questions.key_answer_elements: Labeling and packaging operations must be controlled to prevent mixups; inspection results must be documented.

questions.question: Which provisions of Part 820 are FDA supplements to the incorporated standard rather than incorporation by reference?
questions.iso_clause_title: Control of records; Control of production and service provision; Servicing activities; Identification; Traceability; Complaint handling; Reporting to regulatory authorities
questions.key_answer_elements: 820.10(b)-(e), 820.35 and 820.45 impose FDA requirements in addition to the standard; the balance of the quality system reaches the manufacturer through incorporation by reference.

questions.question: What changed when FDA amended Part 820 to the Quality Management System Regulation, and what is the compliance date?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR Part 820 as amended; QMSR final rule, 89 FR 7523 (February 2, 2024); compliance date February 2, 2026
questions.iso_clause_title: Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes
questions.key_answer_elements: ISO 13485:2016 incorporated by reference; former Subparts C through O reserved; FDA supplements retained at 820.10(b)-(e), 820.35 and 820.45; compliance date February 2, 2026.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR 820.30 require for design controls?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.30 is [Reserved] as of February 2, 2026; design and development requirements now reach the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(c)
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.30 is reserved and route the requirement to 820.10(c) and the standard's design and development clause. Answering as though 820.30 were current is a citation failure.

questions.question: What are the corrective and preventive action requirements of 21 CFR 820.100?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.100 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.100 is reserved and route CAPA to 820.10(a) and the standard's corrective and preventive action clauses.

questions.question: What must a complaint file contain under 21 CFR 820.198?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.198 is [Reserved]; complaint record content is now specified at 21 CFR 820.35(a)
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.198 is reserved and route complaint handling to 820.35(a) and the standard's complaint handling clause.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Device Master Record, a Device History Record, and a Design History File under the current Part 820?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.181, 820.184 and 820.30(j) are [Reserved]; those constructs are not in the current Part 820
questions.iso_clause_title: Medical device file; Control of records; Design and development files
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that the DMR/DHR/DHF terms are not used in the current Part 820 and identify the medical device file, record control and design and development file clauses that carry the equivalent obligations.

questions.question: What are the management responsibility requirements of 21 CFR 820.20?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.20 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.20 is reserved and route management responsibility to 820.10(a) and the standard's management responsibility clause.

questions.question: What are the quality audit requirements of 21 CFR 820.22?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.22 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.22 is reserved and route auditing to 820.10(a) and the standard's internal audit clause.

questions.question: What are the purchasing control and supplier evaluation requirements of 21 CFR 820.50?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.50 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.iso_clause_title: Purchasing; Purchasing process; Purchasing information; Verification of purchased product
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.50 is reserved and route purchasing controls to 820.10(a) and the standard's purchasing clauses.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR 820.75 require for process validation?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.75 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.iso_clause_title: Validation of processes for production and service provision; Particular requirements for validation of processes for sterilization and sterile barrier systems
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.75 is reserved and route process validation to 820.10(a) and the standard's validation clauses.

questions.question: What are the calibration requirements of 21 CFR 820.72 for inspection, measuring, and test equipment?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.72 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.iso_clause_title: Control of monitoring and measuring equipment
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.72 is reserved and route equipment control to 820.10(a) and the standard's monitoring and measuring equipment clause.

questions.question: What statistical techniques does 21 CFR 820.250 require?
questions.expected_citation_draft: TEMPORAL TRAP — 820.250 is [Reserved]; the requirement reaches the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a)
questions.iso_clause_title: Measurement, analysis and improvement — General; Monitoring and measurement of product; Analysis of data
questions.key_answer_elements: Must state that 820.250 is reserved and route statistical technique determination to 820.10(a) and the standard's measurement and analysis clauses.

questions.question: Does Part 820 require a manufacturer to hold ISO 13485 certification, and does a certificate exempt the manufacturer from FDA inspection?
questions.iso_clause_title: Scope; Quality management system — General requirements
questions.key_answer_elements: No certification requirement appears in Part 820; the obligation is to document a QMS complying with the standard. A certificate does not exempt a manufacturer from FDA inspection.

questions.question: Which parts of Title 21 govern device establishment registration, listing, and unique device identification, and how do they interact with Part 820?
questions.key_answer_elements: Registration and listing under Part 807; UDI system under Part 830; Part 820 requires the UDI assignment system and the recording of the UDI.

questions.question: What is the scope of 21 CFR Part 11 and to which records does it apply?
questions.key_answer_elements: Records in electronic form created, modified, maintained, archived, retrieved, or transmitted under predicate rules; electronic signatures; permitted use.

questions.question: What definitions distinguish an open system from a closed system under Part 11?
questions.key_answer_elements: Control of system access by persons responsible for the record content.

questions.question: What controls are required for closed systems under Part 11?
questions.key_answer_elements: Validation, accurate and complete copies, record protection, limiting access, audit trails, operational and authority checks, training, written policies, documentation controls.

questions.question: What are the audit trail requirements under Part 11?
questions.key_answer_elements: Secure computer-generated time-stamped audit trails, independently recorded, no obscuring of previously recorded information, retention and availability for review and copying.

questions.question: What additional controls apply to open systems?
questions.key_answer_elements: All closed-system controls plus measures such as document encryption and digital signature standards to ensure authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality.

questions.question: What must an electronic signature manifestation include when displayed or printed?
questions.key_answer_elements: Printed name of the signer, date and time of signing, meaning of the signature; subject to the same controls as the record.

questions.question: What are the signature/record linking requirements?
questions.key_answer_elements: Signatures linked to their records so they cannot be excised, copied, or transferred to falsify another record.

questions.question: What are the requirements for the uniqueness and certification of electronic signatures?
questions.key_answer_elements: Unique to one individual, not reused or reassigned, identity verification, certification to FDA that electronic signatures are the legally binding equivalent of handwritten signatures.

questions.question: What controls apply to electronic signatures based on identification codes and passwords?
questions.key_answer_elements: Uniqueness of ID/password combination, periodic password aging, loss management, transaction safeguards, testing of devices.

questions.question: A firm uses a cloud-hosted LIMS. Which Part 11 provisions apply to the vendor's controls, and how does the FDA guidance on scope and application affect enforcement discretion?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR 11.10; 11.30; FDA Part 11 Scope and Application guidance (2003)
questions.key_answer_elements: Narrow interpretation of scope, enforcement discretion on validation, audit trails, legacy systems, and record copies; predicate rule requirements remain in effect.

questions.question: Who must comply with the Foreign Supplier Verification Programs regulation and who is the 'importer'?
questions.key_answer_elements: Definition of importer as US owner or consignee at time of entry, or US agent when none, applicability and exemptions.

questions.question: What hazard analysis must an importer conduct under FSVP?
questions.key_answer_elements: Identification of known or reasonably foreseeable hazards, hazard evaluation, reliance on another entity's analysis with review and assessment.

questions.question: What must an importer evaluate about a foreign supplier's performance?
questions.key_answer_elements: Hazard analysis, entity controlling the hazard, supplier procedures and processes, compliance history including FDA warning letters and import alerts, reevaluation every three years or upon new information.

questions.question: What supplier verification activities does FSVP require and how is the appropriate activity determined?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written procedures, annual onsite audit for SAHCODHA hazards unless a written determination supports an alternative, sampling and testing, records review.

questions.question: An importer learns that a foreign supplier failed to control a hazard. What does FSVP require?
questions.key_answer_elements: Prompt appropriate corrective action, investigation, determination whether the FSVP is adequate, and modification as necessary.

questions.question: What identification must an importer provide at entry under FSVP?
questions.key_answer_elements: Name, electronic mail address, and unique facility identifier recognized by FDA for each line of food product offered for import.

questions.question: What are the FSVP recordkeeping requirements including retention period?
questions.key_answer_elements: English language, signed and dated, retention for two years, availability for FDA inspection within 24 hours, electronic records permitted.

questions.question: What is required in a premarket notification 510(k) submission?
questions.key_answer_elements: Device name, establishment registration number, class and classification, proposed labels and labeling, substantial equivalence comparison, 510(k) summary or statement.

questions.question: What is the standard for substantial equivalence and how is it determined?
questions.key_answer_elements: Same intended use, same technological characteristics, or different characteristics that do not raise different questions of safety and effectiveness with supporting performance data.

questions.question: When must a 510(k) be submitted for a change to a legally marketed device?
questions.key_answer_elements: Significant change or modification in design, components, method of manufacture, or intended use; major change in intended use.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 510(k) summary and a 510(k) statement?
questions.key_answer_elements: Summary content requirements and public availability; statement certifying safety and effectiveness information will be made available on request.

questions.question: What must a PMA application contain under Part 814?
questions.key_answer_elements: Summary, device description, manufacturing information, performance standards, nonclinical and clinical investigations, bibliography, samples, labeling, financial certification.

questions.question: What are the PMA supplement requirements and when is a 30-day notice permitted?
questions.key_answer_elements: Changes affecting safety or effectiveness require a supplement; 30-day notice for certain manufacturing process changes; real-time supplement option.

questions.question: What is the De Novo classification process and what must a request contain?
questions.key_answer_elements: Request for classification of a novel device into Class I or II, risk and mitigation discussion, benefit-risk, proposed special controls.

questions.question: How are medical devices classified and what does a 513(g) request accomplish?
questions.key_answer_elements: Class I/II/III definitions and general/special controls; 513(g) request for information on classification and applicable requirements.

questions.question: When is an Investigational Device Exemption required and what are the significant risk criteria?
questions.key_answer_elements: Significant risk vs nonsignificant risk determination, abbreviated requirements, exempt investigations.

questions.question: What are the sponsor responsibilities under an IDE?
questions.key_answer_elements: Selecting qualified investigators, obtaining IRB and FDA approval, monitoring the investigation, maintaining records and reports.

questions.question: What are the establishment registration and device listing requirements and their timing?
questions.key_answer_elements: Who must register, initial and annual registration between October 1 and December 31, listing of devices, fees.

questions.question: What are the unique device identification requirements and what must be submitted to GUDID?
questions.expected_citation_draft: 21 CFR 830 Subpart B and E; 21 CFR 801.20
questions.key_answer_elements: UDI on label and package, direct marking requirements, device identifier and production identifier, GUDID data submission.

questions.question: What events must a device manufacturer report under the Medical Device Reporting regulation and within what timeframe?
questions.key_answer_elements: Death, serious injury, or malfunction that would likely cause or contribute to a death or serious injury; 30-day reports; 5-day reports for events requiring remedial action.

questions.question: What is the difference between a malfunction report and a serious injury report under Part 803?
questions.key_answer_elements: Definitions of serious injury, malfunction, and reportable event; recurrence likelihood standard.

questions.question: What are the MDR written procedure and recordkeeping requirements?
questions.key_answer_elements: Timely and effective identification, communication, and evaluation procedures; standardized review process; MDR event files; retention for two years or expected device life.

questions.question: What are the user facility and importer reporting obligations under Part 803?
questions.key_answer_elements: User facility death reports to FDA and manufacturer, serious injury reports to manufacturer, annual reports; importer reporting duties.

questions.question: When must a device correction or removal be reported to FDA under Part 806?
questions.key_answer_elements: Correction or removal initiated to reduce a risk to health or to remedy a violation that may present a risk to health; report within 10 working days.

questions.question: What corrections and removals are exempt from reporting under Part 806 but still require records?
questions.key_answer_elements: Exemptions including actions already reported under Part 803 or Part 1004; records of non-reportable corrections and removals with rationale.

questions.question: What does Part 7 provide regarding recall classification and firm-initiated recalls?
questions.key_answer_elements: Class I, II, and III definitions, health hazard evaluation, recall strategy, depth of recall, public warning, effectiveness checks, firm-initiated recall notification.

questions.question: What is the difference between a recall, a market withdrawal, and a stock recovery?
questions.key_answer_elements: Violative product subject to legal action vs minor violation not subject to legal action vs product not yet marketed or left the firm's control.

questions.question: What statutory provision governs premarket tobacco product applications, and what must an application contain?
questions.key_answer_elements: Full reports of investigations, statement of components and ingredients, description of methods and controls, samples, labeling, APPH standard.

questions.question: What is the 'appropriate for the protection of the public health' standard and what does FDA consider?
questions.key_answer_elements: Risks and benefits to the population as a whole, including users and nonusers, likelihood of cessation and initiation.

questions.question: What postmarket reporting requirements apply to a marketing granted order under the PMTA rule?
questions.key_answer_elements: Periodic and annual reports, adverse experience reporting, changes to the product, records retention.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Substantial Equivalence report, an Exemption from SE request, and a PMTA?
questions.key_answer_elements: Predicate tobacco product comparison, minor modification exemption criteria, and the independent PMTA pathway.

questions.question: What must a Substantial Equivalence report contain and what is a valid predicate?
questions.key_answer_elements: Commercially marketed in the US as of February 15, 2007 or previously found substantially equivalent; same characteristics or different characteristics not raising different questions of public health.

questions.question: What is a Modified Risk Tobacco Product application and what evidence does it require?
questions.key_answer_elements: Risk modification vs exposure modification orders, consumer perception studies, population health evidence, postmarket surveillance requirement.

questions.question: What are the establishment registration and product listing requirements for tobacco product manufacturers?
questions.key_answer_elements: Registration of domestic establishments, product listing, biannual registration timing, ingredient listing under 904.

questions.question: Which products are subject to FDA tobacco authority under the deeming rule, and what does Part 1100 address?
questions.key_answer_elements: Deemed products including ENDS, cigars, pipe tobacco, hookah; requirements applicable to deemed products.

questions.question: What restrictions apply to the sale and distribution of tobacco products to minors and to free samples?
questions.key_answer_elements: Minimum age verification, photo ID requirement, vending machine restrictions, prohibition on free samples and certain self-service displays.

questions.question: What nicotine addiction warning statement requirements apply to covered tobacco products including ENDS?
questions.key_answer_elements: Required warning text, placement, size, and rotation on packages and advertisements.

questions.question: What tobacco product manufacturing practice requirements has FDA proposed or established, and what is their current status?
questions.key_answer_elements: Statutory authority for good manufacturing practice requirements for tobacco products; status of rulemaking; interim expectations.

questions.question: What ingredient listing and HPHC reporting obligations apply to tobacco product manufacturers?
questions.key_answer_elements: Ingredient listing by brand and sub-brand, harmful and potentially harmful constituent reporting, timing of submissions.

questions.question: What facility registration and product listing obligations does MoCRA impose on cosmetic manufacturers?
questions.key_answer_elements: Facility registration and biennial renewal, product listing with ingredient information, responsible person obligations.

questions.question: What are the cosmetic labeling requirements in Part 701?
questions.key_answer_elements: Ingredient declaration in descending order, principal display panel, name and place of business, net quantity of contents.

questions.question: What warning statement requirements apply to cosmetics whose safety has not been substantiated?
questions.key_answer_elements: Required warning that the safety of the product has not been determined, type size and prominence.

questions.question: Which ingredients are prohibited or restricted in cosmetics under Part 700?
questions.key_answer_elements: Bithionol, mercury compounds, vinyl chloride propellants, halogenated salicylanilides, chloroform, methylene chloride, hexachlorophene, sunscreens in cosmetics.

questions.question: What adverse event reporting obligations does MoCRA create for cosmetic responsible persons?
questions.key_answer_elements: Serious adverse event reports within 15 business days, records retention, contact information on label.

questions.question: What general standards apply to biological products under Part 600 and how do they interact with Part 211?
questions.key_answer_elements: Personnel, physical establishment, equipment, animals and care; both CGMP and Part 600 apply, with the more specific controlling.

questions.question: What adverse experience reporting requirements apply to licensed biological products?
questions.key_answer_elements: 15-day alert reports, periodic adverse experience reports, definitions of serious and unexpected, recordkeeping.

questions.question: What is required for a biologics license application under Part 601?
questions.key_answer_elements: Data derived from nonclinical and clinical studies, manufacturing methods and facility information, labeling, demonstration of safety, purity, and potency.

questions.question: How are manufacturing changes to a licensed biological product reported?
questions.key_answer_elements: Prior approval supplement, changes being effected in 30 days, changes being effected, annual report categories based on potential to affect product quality.

questions.question: What CGMP requirements apply to blood and blood components under Part 606?
questions.key_answer_elements: Personnel, standard operating procedures, records of each significant step, retention periods, look-back requirements.

questions.question: What must appear on a device label with respect to the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor?
questions.key_answer_elements: Name and place of business; conditions under which a distributor's name may be used.

questions.question: What does the device labeling regulation require by 'adequate directions for use'?
questions.key_answer_elements: Directions under which a layperson can use the device safely and for its intended purposes; enumerated elements.

questions.question: How does a prescription device qualify for exemption from the adequate directions for use requirement, and what conditions apply?
questions.key_answer_elements: Prescription statement, labeling limited to practitioner use, adequate information for practitioners, and advertising conditions.

questions.question: What labeling requirements apply to an in vitro diagnostic product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Content of the label and of labeling for IVD products, including intended use, warnings, and performance characteristics.

questions.question: Which section requires that a device label and device package bear a unique device identifier?
questions.key_answer_elements: Labels and packages of every device must bear a UDI unless an exception applies.

questions.question: In what form must a unique device identifier appear on a label?
questions.key_answer_elements: Easily readable plain-text form and automatic identification and data capture technology form.

questions.question: Which devices must be directly marked with a unique device identifier, and what exceptions apply?
questions.key_answer_elements: Devices intended for more than one use and intended to be reprocessed before each use; enumerated exceptions.

questions.question: How does a labeler request an exception from, or an alternative to, a UDI requirement?
questions.key_answer_elements: General exceptions at 801.30; written request for exception or alternative at 801.55, including the criteria FDA applies.

questions.question: What must a unique device identifier consist of under Part 830?
questions.key_answer_elements: Device identifier and, where applicable, production identifiers; issued under a system operated by an FDA-accredited issuing agency.

questions.question: What information must a labeler submit to the Global Unique Device Identification Database, and within what timeframe?
questions.key_answer_elements: Devices subject to identification requirements, the data elements required, and the submission timeframe tied to the labeling date.

questions.question: What does Part 201 require regarding the name and place of business on a drug label?
questions.key_answer_elements: Name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; conditions for use of a distributor's name.

questions.question: What is required by 'adequate directions for use' for a drug product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Directions under which a layperson can use a drug safely for its intended purposes; enumerated elements.

questions.question: What are the content and format requirements for prescription drug labeling under the physician labeling rule?
questions.key_answer_elements: General requirements at 201.56; specific required sections, Highlights, and order of content at 201.57.

questions.question: What are the format and content requirements for the Drug Facts labeling of an over-the-counter drug product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Required Drug Facts headings, order, type size, and graphical specifications.

questions.question: How must the net quantity of contents be declared on a drug label?
questions.key_answer_elements: Placement, units, and prominence of the net quantity statement.

questions.question: Which section governs the placement of the expiration date on a drug label, and which CGMP section requires expiration dating?
questions.key_answer_elements: Location of the expiration date on the label; expiration dating requirement and stability support under the drug CGMP.

questions.question: Which section requires the prescription-only statement on the label of a prescription drug?
questions.key_answer_elements: Conditions for the exemption from adequate directions for use, including the required prescription statement.

questions.question: What bar code requirements apply to the label of a drug product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Linear bar code containing the National Drug Code number; products covered and exemptions.

questions.question: Who must register a drug establishment with FDA, and when must registration occur and be renewed?
questions.key_answer_elements: Establishments engaged in manufacturing, preparation, propagation, compounding, or processing; initial registration timing and annual renewal; information required.

questions.question: What are the drug listing requirements, and how is the National Drug Code assigned?
questions.key_answer_elements: NDC composition and labeler code assignment; drug listing content and timing for submissions.

questions.question: What are the general requirements for informed consent and the basic elements that must be provided to a subject?
questions.key_answer_elements: Legally effective informed consent, comprehension, no exculpatory language; the enumerated basic and additional elements.

questions.question: Under what conditions may an investigation proceed with an exception from informed consent for emergency research?
questions.key_answer_elements: Life-threatening situation, unavailable consent, prospect of direct benefit, IRB findings, community consultation and public disclosure.

questions.question: What additional safeguards apply to children enrolled in a clinical investigation of a drug or device?
questions.key_answer_elements: Risk and benefit categories, IRB findings, assent of the child and permission of parents or guardians.

questions.question: What financial interests and arrangements must a clinical investigator disclose, and who submits the disclosure?
questions.key_answer_elements: Disclosable financial arrangements and interests; the applicant submits certification or disclosure with the marketing application.

questions.question: What are the membership requirements for an institutional review board and the criteria for approval of research?
questions.key_answer_elements: Composition, diversity, non-scientific and unaffiliated members; risk minimization, equitable selection, informed consent, data monitoring.

questions.question: When may an institutional review board use expedited review procedures?
questions.key_answer_elements: Categories of minimal-risk research published by FDA; minor changes to approved research; chairperson or designated reviewer.

questions.question: What are the responsibilities of the study director and the required content of a nonclinical laboratory study protocol?
questions.key_answer_elements: Single point of study control and responsibilities; required protocol elements and approval.

questions.question: What are the retention requirements for records and specimens from a nonclinical laboratory study?
questions.key_answer_elements: Retention periods tied to the type of application and the archive requirements.

questions.question: What must an investigational new drug application contain, and what are the IND safety reporting requirements?
questions.key_answer_elements: Required IND sections; definitions of serious and unexpected suspected adverse reaction; 15-day and 7-day reporting timeframes.

questions.question: How is a significant risk device investigation distinguished from a nonsignificant risk investigation, and what must an IDE application contain?
questions.key_answer_elements: Significant risk definition and the abbreviated requirements pathway; IDE application content and FDA approval.

questions.question: Which farms and produce are covered by the produce safety rule, and what exemptions apply?
questions.key_answer_elements: Covered produce and covered farms, monetary thresholds, qualified exemption and the produce rarely consumed raw exclusion.

questions.question: What requirements apply to agricultural water under the produce safety rule?
questions.key_answer_elements: Water quality, inspection of the water system, testing and corrective measures, and records.

questions.question: What personnel qualification, training, health and hygiene requirements apply under the produce safety rule?
questions.key_answer_elements: Training of personnel handling covered produce, health and hygiene practices, and training records.

questions.question: What registration and process filing obligations apply to a commercial processor of low-acid canned foods?
questions.key_answer_elements: Establishment registration and process filing with FDA; scheduled processes filed before packing.

questions.question: What does Part 113 require with respect to establishing scheduled processes and keeping processing records?
questions.key_answer_elements: Production and process controls, scheduled process establishment by a qualified authority, and processing and production records.

questions.question: What pH control requirements apply to acidified foods?
questions.key_answer_elements: Equilibrium pH control at or below 4.6, monitoring of acidification, and required records.

questions.question: What hazard analysis and HACCP plan requirements apply to juice processors?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written hazard analysis; HACCP plan content, critical control points, critical limits, monitoring, corrective actions and verification.

questions.question: What pathogen reduction performance standard applies to juice, and which section establishes it?
questions.key_answer_elements: A 5-log reduction of the pertinent microorganism, and the process control requirements that support it.

questions.question: What must a seafood HACCP plan contain, and what monitoring and verification are required?
questions.key_answer_elements: HACCP plan content, monitoring procedures, corrective actions, and verification and validation activities.

questions.question: What does the intentional adulteration rule require in a food defense plan?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written food defense plan, vulnerability assessment, mitigation strategies and their explanation.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: Which facilities must register with FDA, and how often must registration be renewed?
questions.key_answer_elements: Domestic and foreign facilities that manufacture, process, pack or hold food for consumption in the United States; biennial renewal.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: Who must establish and maintain records under the records access requirements, and what must those records contain?
questions.key_answer_elements: Persons who manufacture, process, pack, transport, distribute, receive, hold or import food; nonexclusive prior source and subsequent recipient information; retention periods.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: What prior notice must be given for food offered for import, and when must it be submitted?
questions.key_answer_elements: Who must submit, timeframes by mode of transportation, and the required information elements.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: What requirements apply to vehicles and transportation operations under the sanitary transportation rule?
questions.key_answer_elements: Design and maintenance of vehicles and equipment; responsibilities of shippers, loaders, carriers and receivers.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: What training and records requirements apply to carriers under the sanitary transportation rule?
questions.key_answer_elements: Carrier personnel training when the carrier and shipper agree the carrier is responsible for sanitary conditions; record retention periods.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: Which foods are subject to the additional traceability recordkeeping requirements, and what must be recorded?
questions.key_answer_elements: Foods on the Food Traceability List; critical tracking events and key data elements; traceability lot codes.

questions.domain: Food Facility, Records, Transport & Traceability — 21 CFR Part 1
questions.question: What must a traceability plan contain, and how long must traceability records be retained?
questions.key_answer_elements: Traceability plan elements including procedures, lot code assignment and a farm map; record retention and availability to FDA.

questions.question: What current good manufacturing practice requirements apply to the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of animal food?
questions.key_answer_elements: Personnel, plant and grounds, sanitation, water supply and plumbing, equipment and utensils, processes and controls, warehousing and distribution, and holding and distribution of human food by-products.

questions.question: What hazard analysis and preventive controls requirements apply to an animal food facility?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written hazard analysis identifying known or reasonably foreseeable hazards; preventive controls and the preventive control management components.

questions.question: What supply-chain program requirements apply to an animal food facility, and when is the receiving facility responsible for it?
questions.key_answer_elements: Written supply-chain program, supplier approval and verification activities, and the circumstances in which the requirement does not apply.

questions.question: What requirements apply to medicated feed manufacturing and to veterinary feed directive drugs?
questions.key_answer_elements: CGMP for medicated feeds; VFD issuance, content, distribution and recordkeeping.

questions.question: What accreditation and certification requirements apply to a mammography facility?
questions.key_answer_elements: Certificate required to operate; accreditation by an FDA-approved body; personnel qualification requirements.

questions.question: What quality assurance requirements apply to mammography equipment, medical records, and mammography reports?
questions.key_answer_elements: Equipment QA, quality control testing, medical records and mammography reports, medical outcomes audit, and consumer complaint mechanism.

questions.question: What records and reports must a manufacturer of an electronic product subject to a performance standard maintain and submit?
questions.key_answer_elements: Product reports, abbreviated reports, and the records of testing, distribution and quality control to be maintained.

questions.question: What must a manufacturer do when an electronic product is found to have a defect relating to safety or fails to comply with a performance standard?
questions.key_answer_elements: Notification of defect or noncompliance to FDA and to affected persons; repurchase, repair or replacement plans.

questions.question: What performance standard applies to laser products, and what class-based requirements does it impose?
questions.key_answer_elements: Laser product classification, performance requirements, labeling and specific-purpose product requirements.

questions.question: What performance standard applies to sunlamp products and ultraviolet lamps intended for use in them?
questions.key_answer_elements: Timer, exposure schedule, protective eyewear, warning label and irradiance ratio requirements.

questions.question: How is a combination product defined, and which part sets the current good manufacturing practice framework for one?
questions.key_answer_elements: Types of combination products; Part 4 Subpart A applies CGMP to combination products and defines constituent parts.

questions.question: What is the streamlined approach to CGMP compliance for a single-entity or co-packaged combination product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Demonstrating compliance with either the drug CGMP or the device quality system requirements, plus the specified additional provisions from the other.

questions.question: If a combination product manufacturer operates a drug CGMP-based system, which device quality system provisions must also be satisfied?
questions.iso_clause_title: Design and development; Purchasing; Installation activities; Servicing activities; Corrective action; Preventive action
questions.key_answer_elements: The enumerated device provisions added to a drug-based system. SME to confirm how Part 4 cross-references read following the February 2, 2026 restructuring of Part 820.

questions.question: What postmarket safety reporting requirements apply to a combination product applicant?
questions.key_answer_elements: Applicable safety reporting requirements by constituent part, five-day and malfunction reporting, and shared reporting responsibilities.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR require for greenhouse gas emissions reporting at a manufacturing facility?
questions.expected_citation_draft: NOT COVERED IN TITLE 21 — required response form: 'Greenhouse gas emissions reporting is not covered in 21 CFR.'
questions.key_answer_elements: Must restate the subject and close flat. Must NOT redirect the user to FDA guidance, another agency, or any alternative source as though it supplied the requirement.

questions.question: What harmful and potentially harmful constituent data must be submitted for a tobacco product?
questions.key_answer_elements: Primary answer cites the regulation. The analyte list is elaboration and is not to be presented as the source of the requirement in the first-tier answer.

questions.question: Give me the specific list of harmful and potentially harmful constituents FDA expects to be tested.
questions.expected_citation_draft: Guidance tier — citation must give the document title, draft or final status, and issue date, and must carry FDA's own disclaimer language from the cited document
questions.key_answer_elements: Second-tier elaboration permitted only after the requirement has been established from the regulation. Guidance must not be characterized as creating the requirement.

questions.question: Is there FDA guidance on shelf-life testing for dietary supplements, and if so, what does it require?
questions.expected_citation_draft: Requirement source is the regulation; guidance is elaboration only — any guidance cited must be identified as draft or final with title and issue date, and carry FDA's disclaimer language
questions.key_answer_elements: Must not state that a guidance document requires anything. Must identify the governing regulation, or state plainly that the regulation does not impose the requirement.

questions.question: Which FDA guidance requires a device manufacturer to qualify its suppliers?
questions.expected_citation_draft: FALSE PREMISE — the requirement traces to 21 CFR 820.10(a) and the incorporated standard, not to a guidance document
questions.key_answer_elements: Must correct the premise: guidance does not create the requirement. Must route the obligation to the regulation and the standard's purchasing clauses.

questions.question: What does 21 CFR say about the content of a risk management file under ISO 14971?
questions.expected_citation_draft: ISO 14971 is not incorporated by reference into Part 820; risk management obligations reach the manufacturer through 21 CFR 820.10(a) and the incorporated standard
questions.key_answer_elements: Must distinguish the standard incorporated by reference at 820.7(b) from standards that are not. Must not present ISO 14971 as a Title 21 requirement.

questions.question: What are the record retention requirements?
questions.expected_citation_draft: AMBIGUOUS — retention periods differ by part; the platform must ask which sector or part applies rather than selecting one
questions.key_answer_elements: Must request the governing part or sector. Selecting a single part and answering as though it were the question is a completeness failure.

questions.question: Our quality manual is built around the Subpart structure of the Quality System Regulation. Confirm that Subparts C through O still apply so I can leave it as it is.
questions.expected_citation_draft: FALSE PREMISE — Subparts C through O are [Reserved] as of February 2, 2026
questions.iso_clause_title: Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes
questions.key_answer_elements: Must correct the premise rather than confirm it, and must not advise that no action is required. Must not guarantee a compliance outcome either way.

questions.question: In plain English, why must a device manufacturer investigate a complaint, and what requires it?
questions.key_answer_elements: Plain-English explanation delivered with the citation attached. A correct explanation carrying no citation is a citation failure under the rubric.

questions.question: Summarize the requirements of 21 CFR 111.900.
